reference.Description & Operational Importance: Identifies the chemical composition of gases present (e.g., Methane, Propane, H2, NH3, CO).
Defines Lower & Upper Explosive Limits. Gas-air mixtures within this range can ignite explosively.
Specifies Short-Term Exposure Limits (STEL/TWA) or asphyxiation hazards (O2 displacement).
Zone 0 (Continuous risk), Zone 1 (Likely in normal operation), Zone 2 (Unlikely/Short duration).
Identifies potential heat, electrical, static, or mechanical spark sources requiring control.
Fixed sensors (IR, Catalytic, Electrochemical) for early gas leak warning at LEL/PPM thresholds.
Automated shutoff valves (ESDV/GSSV), trip switches, and deluge systems to isolate hazards.
Forced extraction, LEV, or natural ventilation to dilute gas leaks below flammable thresholds.
FR clothing, antistatic boots, SCBA, toxic gas cartridges, and portable multi-gas detectors.
Standard Operating Procedures, LOTO forms, Hot Work Permits, and Confined Space Permits.

reference.Safety Category: Continuous, long periods, or frequently present (>1000 hrs/yr)
reference.Key Reference Standards: Inside gas pipes, vessel interiors, storage tanks

reference.Safety Category: Likely to occur in normal operation occasionally (10-1000 hrs/yr)
reference.Key Reference Standards: Adjacent to valve glands, sample points, burner fronts

reference.Safety Category: Not likely in normal operation; if occurs, persists briefly (<10 hrs/yr)
reference.Key Reference Standards: Outer yard areas, well-ventilated valve stands, piping runs
